newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks down a shade in dead slow start.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks down a shade in dead slow start.

text.p: Mexican stocks inched down at the open on Friday amid dead slow trade due to the absence of U.S. investors, dealers said.
"The market is dead on its feet. We're effectively on vacation," a desk trader said.

"It's very quiet, there is some selling carried over from the close yesterday, and some who are buying, but it's flat, there's no point in buying high today. There's nothing to move the market," a floor trader added.
The leading IPC share index was down 0.77 point in the opening minutes of trade, or 0.02 percent, at 4,590.85.
Trading volume was lifeless at 230,000 shares.
Dealers said the mild downward bias was a continuation of profit-taking begun on Thursday, after Wall Street closed early ahead of the U.S. Independence Day holiday.
Construction firm Empresas ICA and cement maker Cemex weighed most on the market, traders said. ICA was down 80 centavos at 135.50 pesos, while Cemex was off 10 centavos at 39.80.
Dealers said volume was too thin to reflect a trend, however.
"What trends? No one wants to do anything. Just look at Bancomer and Telmex," a desk trader said
Financial firm Bancomer and telecom Telefonos de Mexico (Telmex), both market heavyweights, were flat. Bancomer traded at 4.01 pesos and Telmex at 19.70 pesos.
On the broad market, decliners outnumbered gainers by nine to two, out of 23 stocks traded.
